Gergonne And Soddy

GeometryTrianglesCircles
Game: Move the three corners of a triangle and watch two special lines that always cross at a right angle.
How to play: Drag a corner, or focus it and use the arrow keys. Press the buttons to show the circle, the helper lines, the right-angle mark or the flipped circles.
Look for the math

Move any corner and both lines swing around, yet the angle where they meet never changes. That is the whole surprise: a right angle that survives every triangle you can draw.

Two lines inside a triangle

The incircle touches the three sides at A₁, B₁, C₁. Join each touch point to the opposite corner: those three cevians meet at the Gergonne point Ge. The lines B₁C₁, C₁A₁ and A₁B₁ meet the sides again at three points called Nobbs' points; they lie on one straight line, the Gergonne line. The line through Ge and the incenter I is the Soddy line. Blue is the Gergonne line; red is the Soddy line.

The page's claim, checked

The original page says: “Wherever the Soddy line is uniquely defined (in particular, in a scalene triangle), it is perpendicular to Gergonne Line.” The logic test measured the angle between the two lines in 2,590 triangles from a grid and a fixed random seed. It was 90° to within 0.001° in every one. The three Nobbs points were collinear and the three cevians passed through Ge in all of those cases too.

The page also says I and Ge never coincide in a scalene triangle. That is true, and a little more is true: they coincide exactly when the triangle is equilateral. An isosceles but not equilateral triangle still has two different points, hence a well-defined Soddy line. The applet refuses to draw the red line when the two points are less than two pixels apart; this page keeps that guard.

Why inversion sees the right angle

Invert the whole picture in the incircle, with radius r and centre I. A line at distance d from I becomes a circle through I, centred halfway from I towards the line's foot, with radius r²/(2d). So:

AB, BC, CA → circles with diameters IC₁, IA₁, IB₁
A₁B₁, B₁C₁, C₁A₁ → circles with diameters CI, AI, BI
the Soddy line IGe → itself
the Gergonne line → the circle with diameter IGe

The last circle contains Ge and the inverted images of all three Nobbs points; the logic test checks all of that, along with the two diameter formulas above. An inversion preserves angles, so a line through the centre of that circle — the Soddy line IGe — is perpendicular to the circle. Inverting back turns it into the perpendicular pair you see on the board. Press Inversions to watch the seven image circles appear.

The switches

The applet has four checkboxes: names, premises, statement and inversions. The original page embeds it twice: once with none of them ticked, and again in the proof with names and statement on. This page opens in that second view. Reset diagram is a convenience added here: the applet had no reset button. When the three corners are nearly in a straight line, the construction runs off the board and the picture is hidden until you move one back.

Press Inversions, then drag one corner close to the line through the other two. The image circles grow enormous, but the red and blue lines still cross at a right angle.
